Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector covers the extraction, processing, and trading of raw and intermediate materials, spanning metals and mining, industrial and specialty chemicals, construction materials such as cement and ready-mixed concrete, and paper and forest products. Reflecting Singapore's role as a regional commodity trading and processing hub rather than a resource-extraction economy, many of the listed companies operate as traders, processors, or regional operators, with metals and minerals forming one of the core commodity groups under Enterprise Singapore's Global Trader Programme. Oversight is distributed across the sector's industries, with the Singapore Chemical Industry Council (SCIC) supporting the chemical industry and the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) regulating construction materials.
Consumer Non-Cyclicals: The Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector covers producers, processors, and retailers of essential goods that consumers purchase regardless of economic conditions, spanning agribusiness and palm oil, packaged food and beverages, and food retail such as supermarkets and convenience stores. Reflecting Singapore's position as a regional agribusiness and commodity hub, several of the largest listed companies are agri-commodity producers and traders operating across Southeast Asia, with agri-commodities forming one of the core groups under Enterprise Singapore's Global Trader Programme. Domestic food retail and food safety are overseen by the Singapore Food Agency (SFA), the statutory board responsible for food safety and security from import through to retail.
Transportation & Logistics: The Transportation & Logistics sector covers the movement of people and goods across air, land, and sea, including passenger airlines, public bus and rail operators, shipping lines, and aviation and freight logistics providers. The industry is regulated by the Ministry of Transport (MOT) through its statutory boards, with the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) overseeing aviation, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) overseeing bus and rail, and the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) overseeing shipping and ports.
Healthcare: The Healthcare sector covers the full range of medical and health-related activities, including hospitals and medical service providers, dental and specialist clinics, pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical companies, medical device and glove manufacturers, and consumer health products. Healthcare services in Singapore are regulated by the Ministry of Health (MOH) under the Healthcare Services Act, while health products such as medicines, medical devices, and complementary medicines are regulated by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA), a statutory board under MOH.
Energy: The Energy sector covers the exploration, production, refining, and trading of oil, gas, and coal, along with the offshore and marine services, rigs, and equipment that support the upstream industry. Reflecting Singapore's position as a regional oil refining, trading, and bunkering hub, the listed companies are concentrated in upstream oil and gas exploration and production, offshore and oilfield services, and fuel trading, with energy forming one of the core commodity groups under Enterprise Singapore's Global Trader Programme. Domestically, the electricity and gas markets are regulated by the Energy Market Authority (EMA), a statutory board under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, though most of the listed companies here operate in upstream oil and gas and offshore services rather than the domestic power market.
Properties & Real Estate: The Properties & Real Estate sector covers the development, investment, management, and brokerage of residential, commercial, and industrial property, including property developers, real estate investment and holding companies, and real estate agencies. Real estate activity in Singapore is overseen by several bodies under the Ministry of National Development, with the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) serving as the national land use planner and the Council for Estate Agencies (CEA) regulating property agencies and agents.
Utilities: The Utilities sector covers companies engaged in the generation, distribution, and supply of essential services including electricity, gas, water, and waste and environmental management. Singapore's energy and gas industries are regulated by the Energy Market Authority (EMA) under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, water supply and reclamation fall under PUB, Singapore's National Water Agency, under the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, while waste and environmental services are overseen by the National Environment Agency (NEA).
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector covers producers and distributors of food, beverages, and other non-cyclical consumer staples, spanning packaged food manufacturers, agribusiness and plantation operators, and consumer-facing services such as education. Singapore's food industry is regulated by the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) under the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, while the sector's education providers fall under separate oversight, with private education institutions regulated by SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and early childhood operators by the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA).
Financial Services: The Financial Services sector encompasses banks, insurers, financial holding companies, capital market intermediaries, and specialty finance providers offering credit, brokerage, and investment services. The industry is regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), which serves as the country's central bank and integrated financial regulator overseeing banking, insurance, securities, and financial advisory activities.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector covers telecommunications network operators, media and entertainment production companies, and content distribution platforms. The industry is regulated by the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) under the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, which oversees both telecommunications licensing and media content standards under a converged regulatory framework.
Infrastructures: The Infrastructures sector covers essential physical and digital networks, including land transport operators, telecommunications and fibre broadband infrastructure, aviation ground handling and engineering services, and shipbuilding. Singapore's telecommunications infrastructure is regulated by the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) under the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, while transport-related infrastructure falls under the Ministry of Transport (MOT) through its statutory boards, with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) overseeing bus and rail, the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) overseeing aviation, and the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) overseeing shipping and shipbuilding.
REIT: The REIT sector comprises real estate investment trusts and stapled trusts that own and manage income-producing property across retail, office, industrial, logistics, hospitality, healthcare, and data centre real estate, both in Singapore and internationally. REITs are regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) under the Securities and Futures Act and the Code on Collective Investment Schemes, with REIT managers required to hold a capital markets services licence.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector covers businesses whose performance is closely tied to discretionary consumer spending, including hospitality and hotels, integrated resorts and gaming, food and beverage retail, jewelry and pawnbroking, general retail, and automotive-related distribution. Hotels and hospitality operators are regulated by the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) through the Hotels Licensing Board (HLB), while casino and gaming operations fall under the Gambling Regulatory Authority of Singapore (GRA), which oversees Singapore's two licensed integrated resorts. Food and beverage retailers are separately regulated by the Singapore Food Agency (SFA), and pawnbroking businesses are licensed through the Registry of Pawnbrokers under the Ministry of Law.
Industrials: The Industrials sector spans a broad range of businesses, including marine and shipbuilding, construction and engineering, diversified conglomerates, postal and logistics services, and defense and aerospace. Marine and shipbuilding activities are regulated by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA), while construction and engineering firms fall under the Building and Construction Authority (BCA), both under the Ministry of Transport and Ministry of National Development respectively. Postal services are separately regulated by the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) under the Postal Services Act.
Technology: The Technology sector covers semiconductor and electronics manufacturing, test and automation equipment, electronics manufacturing services (EMS), and information technology and software companies. Unlike sectors with a dedicated licensing regulator, Singapore's technology and electronics manufacturing industry operates under general business, workplace safety, and environmental regulations, while the Economic Development Board (EDB) drives investment and infrastructure development for the sector rather than direct regulatory oversight.
